articles.title: Vi launches India's first prepaid family plan with data sharing - Indian Broadcasting World
articles.content: New Delhi,16 Oct 2026, By IBW Team Vodafone Idea (Vi) has launched what it describes as India’s first prepaid family plan, allowing customers to form family groups, share mobile data and receive discounts on recharges through the Vi app. The new offering enables up to four Vi prepaid subscribers to join a family group, with one primary member and up to three secondary members. Each member retains their individual prepaid plan and validity while gaining the flexibility to share data with other members, regardless of where they are in the country. Under the proposition, family members can transfer 500 MB of data at a time to another member who is running low. The initiative aims to address a common prepaid user concern, particularly when data is needed for online classes, video calls, navigation and other essential digital services. Vi said all active prepaid subscribers can create a family group through its app. The service also allows members across different telecom circles to join the same family, extending the benefits beyond geographical boundaries. In addition to data sharing, every family member is eligible for guaranteed discounts of up to 10 percent on each recharge made through the Vi app. The company said the offering combines shared connectivity, family management features and exclusive rewards. Speaking about the launch, Avneesh Khosla, Chief Marketing Officer at Vi, said the initiative reflects the company’s focus on making prepaid services more flexible and relevant to customers’ everyday needs. “At Vi, we believe the best innovations are often rooted in simple human truths. We believe the future of prepaid is not just about offering more data but about giving customers greater flexibility on how they use it,” Khosla said. He added that the plan challenges the traditional approach to prepaid mobile services and reinforces the company’s commitment to making connectivity more inclusive. The launch builds on Vi’s brand proposition, ‘Vi Pe Sab Hain VIP’, which focuses on making benefits accessible to a wider range of customers. To promote the new offering, Vi has rolled out a campaign featuring Shah Rukh Khan. The campaign film depicts how the prepaid family plan helps keep his family connected despite members being spread across different cities in India. articles.title: India's first private-built warship INS Samarthak commissioned into Navy - Firstpost
articles.content: Built by Larsen and Toubro, the vessel will support maritime surveillance, weapons trials, unmanned systems operations and humanitarian missions. India's first multi-purpose vessel, INS Samarthak, built by a private shipyard, was commissioned into the Indian Navy on Friday, marking a significant step in the country's efforts to strengthen indigenous warship construction and achieve defence self-reliance. The commissioning ceremony was held at the Navy's base in Karwar, Karnataka, in the presence of Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan. Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan and Karnataka Labour Minister Santosh Lad also attended the event. Built by Larsen and Toubro (L&T) at its Kattupalli shipyard in Tamil Nadu under the Government of India's Make in India initiative, Samarthak has more than 75 per cent indigenous content. Addressing the ceremony, Admiral Swaminathan described the commissioning as an important milestone in India's pursuit of Aatmanirbharata (self-reliance). He said the vessel had been designed, engineered and built in-house at L&T's Warship Design Centre and shipyard. "Samarthak is the first major or big warship contracted to and constructed by a private shipyard to be commissioned into the Indian Navy," he said. Samarthak is the first of the multi-purpose vessels being inducted into the Navy and is expected to play an important role in supporting strategically significant maritime operations. Designed primarily for maritime surveillance and patrol, Samarthak can undertake a range of operational and support roles, including Low Intensity Maritime Operations (LIMO), trials of indigenous weapons and sensors, and operations involving unmanned and autonomous systems. The vessel can function as a target deployment and trials platform, as well as a mothership for unmanned and autonomous systems. It is equipped with a state-of-the-art dynamic positioning system and can launch and recover targets used during warship exercises at sea. Admiral Swaminathan said the vessel would help the Navy test and evaluate indigenous weapons and sensors under development, allowing emerging technologies to be incorporated into operational capabilities more quickly. "These capabilities are particularly vital in today's rapidly evolving technological milieu, where shortening the journey from prototype to production is critical to maintaining the operational edge at sea," he said. The vessel's endurance and ability to support other ships at sea will also help sustain naval operations across dispersed areas of interest for extended periods, the Navy chief said. Its integrated combat suite combines indigenous sensors, weapons and electronic systems designed for operations in challenging maritime environments. Beyond its combat-support and testing roles, Samarthak is equipped to undertake humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) operations, support non-combatant evacuation missions and provide assistance to ships in distress. The vessel has heavy-towing facilities, medical infrastructure and firefighting capabilities to respond to emergencies at sea. It can also be converted into a limited hospital ship, extending its utility during humanitarian missions and other contingencies. Admiral Swaminathan said Samarthak would strengthen the Navy's operational readiness, help translate emerging technologies into operational capabilities and reinforce India's role as a first responder and preferred security partner in the region, in line with the national vision of Mahasagar....

articles.title: India's first uCT Orion Elite CT scanner with calcium scoring comes to Delhi by City Imaging ...
articles.content: Patients in Delhi can now access the uCT Orion Elite, an 80-slice AI-enabled multi-slice non-cardiac CT system installed at City Imaging & Clinical Labs’ Dwarka centre. The installation marks the first CT system from United Imaging to be introduced in the country. The system combines DELTA, a deep-learning algorithm, with Karl3D hybrid iterative reconstruction to enhance image quality. It also features Motion Freeze AI technology to reduce blurring caused by head movement, dual AI cameras to assist with patient positioning and monitoring, and automated image-quality checks. The system also supports ECG-gated calcium scoring. Remaining still during a CT scan can be difficult for children, elderly patients and people experiencing pain or discomfort. The scanner’s Motion Freeze technology is designed to correct different types of head movement, including rotation, translation and oscillation, helping reduce motion-related artefacts that can affect image clarity. Based on deep-learning technology, the algorithm is designed to correct movement-related distortions and support clearer images. Its DELTA technology uses a deep-learning-trained algorithm to enhance image quality and help reduce image noise, supporting clearer visualisation of anatomical structures. The uCT Orion Elite combines DELTA with Karl3D, a hybrid iterative reconstruction technology. This combination is described by the manufacturer as an industry-first integration in a CT system. The scanner supports tube voltage settings ranging from 60 kV to 140 kV and image reconstruction at a matrix size of 1024 × 1024. Dr Aakar Kapoor, Founder & Partner & Consultant Radiologist, City Imaging & Clinical Labs, Delhi, said, “The focus of diagnostic imaging is not just on adopting advanced technology, but on making it clinically useful and accessible to patients. With the uCT Orion Elite, we are expanding our imaging capabilities while introducing calcium scoring on a non-cardiac CT platform. This reflects our approach to investing in technology that supports clinical assessment, strengthens diagnostic capabilities and addresses a wider range of patient needs at a single centre.” The system also uses dual AI cameras, positioned above the scanner and inside its bore, to assist with patient positioning and movement monitoring. Its AI-based Qcheck quality-control platform can flag issues such as patient movement, metal-related artefacts, respiratory motion and scan-range errors. Additional features include checks related to lead-apron use and potential gantry collisions. These tools help technologists monitor the scanning process, identify potential issues and maintain consistent procedures, while trained staff remain responsible for patient safety. The uCT Orion Elite includes an AI-based feature that can flag head CT images that may indicate bleeding within the skull. An alert draws the operator’s attention to a suspected finding for further clinical review, potentially helping the care team identify urgent cases for timely assessment. The scanner’s ECG-gated calcium scoring provides an additional assessment option for eligible patients. The system automatically identifies and marks calcified areas and generates measurements, including a calcium score, along with volume and mass calculations. Doctors can interpret these results alongside a patient’s age, medical history and other risk factors. With the new installation, City Imaging & Clinical Labs aims to make advanced...

articles.title: Aditya-L1 and Proba-3 Study Solar Eruptions - GKToday
articles.content: Home Aditya-L1 and Proba-3 Study Solar Eruptions Aditya-L1 and Proba-3 Study Solar Eruptions October 16, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 On 16 October 2026, India’s Aditya-L1 mission and the European Space Agency’s (ESA) Proba-3 mission combined observations of solar eruptions. Data from Aditya-L1 ’s Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) and Proba-3’s ASPIICS instrument were used to measure the mass, density and energy of coronal mass ejections (CMEs) near the Sun. Solar Flares and Coronal Mass Ejections Solar flares are sudden releases of energy from the Sun’s atmosphere, while CMEs are large expulsions of plasma and magnetic field from the solar corona. Both phenomena can affect space weather and Earth’s near-space environment. In 2026, an Aditya-L1 study identified small, short-lived brightenings in the solar atmosphere hours before major flares; these brightenings clustered around the eventual flare site. Researchers from the Manipal Centre for Natural Sciences, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, ISRO and the Department of Space conducted the study. On 23 July 2026, Aditya-L1 observations were reported to include a comprehensive analysis of photospheric iron fluorescence across 47 X-class flares during the 2024 peak of Solar Cycle 25. The observations also provided spectroscopic signatures of the onset phase of a CME. Aditya-L1 and Solar Observation Aditya-L1 is India’s first dedicated solar mission. ISRO launched it on 2 September 2023, and the spacecraft entered a halo orbit around the Sun–Earth L1 point on 6 January 2024. A halo orbit around L1 provides a continuous view of the Sun. L1 is the first of five Lagrange points in the Sun–Earth system. Proba-3 and Formation Flying ESA’s Proba-3 is a two-spacecraft mission launched by ISRO’s PSLV-XL rocket on 5 December 2024. Its spacecraft fly in precise formation to create artificial solar eclipses, allowing observations of the faint corona. On 1 January 2026, ESA confirmed that the mission had achieved autonomous formation flying with millimetre-level precision. By 17 December 2025, it had produced more than 50 artificial eclipses and over 250 hours of high-resolution coronal video. Important Facts for Exams Proba-3’s ASPIICS instrument observes the solar corona using an artificial eclipse created by the spacecraft formation. Aditya-L1 carries the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph, designed to observe the solar corona. Proba-3’s first scientific results, published in March 2026, found inner-corona solar-wind structures travelling three to four times faster than earlier estimates. ISRO and ESA held a solar-science workshop at the Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology in Thiruvananthapuram from 19 to 23 January 2026. The Solar Orbiter mission also contributed complementary data presented at the January 2026 workshop. Aditya-L1 and Proba-3 use different observing approaches to study the Sun’s corona and related solar activity. articles.title: VFS Global Opens Northeast India's First Visa Application Centre in Guwahati, to Serve ...
articles.content: Updated 16 October 2026 at 11:31 IST VFS Global has opened Northeast India's first visa application centre in Guwahati, inaugurated by Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma. The facility will serve applicants from all eight Northeastern states and initially process visa applications for 14 countries, including the UK, France, Italy and Japan. Initiative Desk Initiatives News 3 min read Follow : VFS Global Opens Northeast India's First Visa Centre in GuwahatiVFS Global Opens Northeast India's First Visa Centre in Guwahati | Image: VFS Global Guwahati: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Thursday inaugurated the first VFS Global Visa Application Centre in Assam at the Inter-State Bus Terminus (ISBT), Khanapara, Guwahati, marking a significant step towards improving access to international visa services for applicants across the Northeast. The centre was jointly inaugurated by Sarma, Assam Tourism Minister Ajanta Neog, Transport Minister Charan Boro, and Yummi Talwar, Chief Operating Officer, South Asia, VFS Global. The ceremony was also attended by representatives of the diplomatic missions of Switzerland, the Czech Republic, Italy and France. The new facility will serve applicants from all eight Northeastern states — Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura and Sikkim — and will initially facilitate visa applications for 14 countries: Austria, Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Egypt, Estonia, France, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Malta, Morocco, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. The centre will also accept Malta D-visa applications. The facility will provide access to Schengen visa application services, enabling eligible applicants to apply for travel to the Schengen Area, which comprises 29 European countries. Its modern infrastructure, technology-enabled processes and customer support services are intended to make the application process more convenient and organised. Advertisement Speaking at the inauguration, Chief Minister Sarma said the centre's significance extended beyond Guwahati, as it would make visa application services more accessible to people across the entire Northeastern region. He emphasised that VFS Global would facilitate only the visa application process, while the decision to grant or refuse a visa would remain solely with the respective governments and diplomatic missions. Advertisement “The value of this facility lies in making access to the process easier while maintaining the required procedure,” Sarma said. The Chief Minister also highlighted the role of the Centre's Act East policy under Prime Minister Narendra Modi in positioning the Northeast at the heart of India's engagement with its eastern neighbours. He said improved infrastructure, better connectivity and stronger economic cooperation were creating new opportunities for Assam in trade, investment, tourism, education and innovation. Sarma added that the government's responsibility was to translate these emerging possibilities into tangible benefits for the people of the state, particularly by strengthening opportunities for young people, supporting businesses and encouraging international engagement. Yummi Talwar, Chief Operating Officer, South Asia, VFS Global, said the new centre would strengthen access to visa services for applicants across Assam and the wider Northeast, amid growing aspirations related to education, business, tourism and international mobility. articles.title: Mormugao Port secures India's first private 5G network authorisation - Indian Infrastructure
articles.content: Mormugao Port Authority (MPA) has become India’s first major port and government autonomous body to secure authorisation for a captive non-public network (CNPN) to establish a private 5G network. Granted by the Department of Telecommunications in September 2026 under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, the authorisation is valid for 20 years. The proposed network will support smart port operations, automated logistics, cargo tracking, real-time monitoring, drone surveillance and smart sensors. MPA has appointed a consultant to prepare a detailed project report and issued a request for information to identify system integrators and equipment manufacturers. proof-of-concept trials are under way. articles.title: India's family offices bet on homegrown AI firms to gain ground
articles.content: India’s family offices bet on homegrown AI firms to gain ground At least six homegrown companies have amassed valuations of more than $1 billion, underscoring the emergence of a new generation of technology firms as AI adoption accelerates among Indian consumers and businesses. Bloomberg Published On Oct 16, 2026 at 09:32 AM IST Select ETEnterpriseAI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook India still faces a significant funding shortfall. Private investment in its AI economy totaled more than $15 billion between 2013 and 2025, according to Stanford University’s AI Index Report. The artificial intelligence boom has cemented US and Chinese tech dominance and created fortunes across North Asia’s chip supply chain. Now, India’s billionaire family offices and wealthy investors are betting on homegrown startups to gain ground in the global AI race. At least six homegrown companies have amassed valuations of more than $1 billion, underscoring the emergence of a new generation of technology firms as AI adoption accelerates among Indian consumers and businesses. Advt Billionaire tech founder Azim Premji ’s family office, WhatsApp Inc.’s Chief Executive Officer Kunal Shah’s QED Innovation Labs and Manipal Group Chairman Ranjan Pai’s family office are among the investors leading the push into such startups. India still faces a significant funding shortfall. Private investment in its AI economy totaled more than $15 billion between 2013 and 2025, according to Stanford University’s AI Index Report. This compared with $757 billion investment in the US and nearly $132 billion in China’s AI ecosystem. That has left an opening for billionaire families, conglomerates and venture investors to fund a homegrown AI industry. “Several family offices and angel investors now are keen on investing directly as they get comfortable with how India’s AI ecosystem is coming into place,” said Riddhiman Jain, head of investments at Indian wealth manager Waterfield Advisors. “AI needs patient capital, which is scarce, and the investing universe is still at a very early stage.” Premji Invest has emerged as the biggest Indian family office investing across the AI landscape globally. Most recently in June, it invested in a $27 million round in AI verification platform Pramaana Labs, founded by alumni of the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (Chennai). Advt The investment firm’s portfolio ranges from multibillion-dollar AI and technology platforms globally such as Databricks and Canva to generative-AI startups Spotdraft and Writer, according to Tracxn. Billionaire doctor-turned-entrepreneur Pai’s family office, Claypond Capital, has stepped up its investments this year. It participated in content startup Flam’s $40 million round in September and backed vibe coding platform Emergent’s $130 million round in July. The influx of capital is helping create a new crop of firms spanning AI models, enterprise software, coding and other applications. articles.title: Vishvajit More wins India's first U23 world Greco-Roman silver - The News Mill
articles.content: ANI Photo | Vishvajit More wins India’s first U23 world Greco-Roman silver Vishvajit More made history for Indian wrestling by securing the country’s first silver medal in Greco-Roman wrestling at the U23 World Championships in Las Vegas on October 15. Having previously won two bronze medals at this event, More advanced to a higher podium position after a closely contested final. Georgia’s Koba Karumidze claimed the gold with a 13–12 victory, leaving More just one point short of the title, according to a press release from the U23 World Wrestling Championships. Add TNM on Google More began his campaign by defeating Mexico’s Isaac Marin Mata 10–8, then overcame Iranian U20 world champion Armin Shamsipour 8–1 in the quarterfinals. He secured his first appearance in a title bout with a 7–4 victory against Russia’s Malik Gigiev in the semifinals. In the women’s competition, Vaishnavi Patil (65kg) and Amruta Pujari (72kg) progressed to the quarterfinals, with Pujari receiving a first-round bye. Komal and Diksha Malik remained in contention for bronze medals. Komal will compete for bronze after losing to Ukraine’s Alina Filipovych by technical superiority in the semifinals, while Diksha continues her medal campaign in the 76kg category. ADVERTISEMENT Mansi Lather exited the women’s 68kg competition following a narrow 9–10 quarterfinal defeat to Italy’s Laura Godino. In other Greco-Roman results, Chetan (63kg) was eliminated in the pre-quarterfinals and Karan Kamboj (87kg) lost by technical superiority in the qualification round. articles.title: Modi Launches Five Development Projects Worth ₹3350 Crore in Ladakh - GKToday
articles.content: Home Modi Launches Five Development Projects Worth ₹3,350 Crore in Ladakh Modi Launches Five Development Projects Worth ₹3,350 Crore in Ladakh October 15, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 On 15 October 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi virtually inaugurated or dedicated five development projects in Ladakh, valued at approximately ₹3,350 crore. The package covers transport connectivity, power infrastructure, cultural heritage conservation and water security. The initiatives include an airport terminal, a road through the Zanskar Valley, energy projects, a petroglyph park and water bodies developed under Project Him Sarovar. Infrastructure and Connectivity The New Passenger Terminal Building at Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport in Leh was constructed at a cost of ₹640 crore. Spread across 23,800 square metres, it is designed to handle 35 lakh passengers annually and uses geothermal energy for improved energy efficiency. The 298-kilometre Nimmu-Padum-Darcha Road, built by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO), provides an alternative road corridor to Ladakh through the remote Zanskar Valley. The BRO is a road-development organisation under the Ministry of Defence and undertakes infrastructure work in border areas. Petroglyph Conservation India’s first Petroglyph Conservation Park was inaugurated at Sindhu Ghat in Leh. Petroglyphs are images or designs carved, pecked or engraved into rock surfaces; Ladakh contains prehistoric rock carvings that form part of its archaeological heritage. Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena laid the park’s foundation stone on 18 April 2026, observed as World Heritage Day. By 29 June 2026, ancient carvings were being systematically relocated from vulnerable sites across Ladakh, and the park was targeted for completion by September 2026. Energy and Water Security The nine-megawatt Hanu Small Hydroelectric Project and the 66-kilovolt, double-circuit Dah-Hanu-Khaltsi Transmission Line were among the inaugurated power infrastructure projects. Hydroelectric projects generate electricity using water flow, while transmission lines carry electricity from generating facilities to distribution networks. The Prime Minister also inaugurated 40 water bodies developed across 40 villages under Project Him Sarovar. The project’s water bodies form part of the development package’s water-security initiatives. Important Facts for Exams Ladakh became a Union Territory on 31 October 2019, following the reorganisation of the former State of Jammu and Kashmir. The Border Roads Organisation was established in 1960 and operates under the Ministry of Defence. Petroglyphs are rock engravings or carvings and are distinct from pictographs, which are painted or drawn on rock surfaces. World Heritage Day is observed annually on 18 April and is also known as the International Day for Monuments and Sites. Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport serves Leh, the principal town of Ladakh. The Nimmu-Padum-Darcha Road connects the region through the Zanskar Valley. articles.title: Modi inaugurates five key projs worth Rs 3,350 crore in Ladakh - MillenniumPost
articles.content: New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday virtually inaugurated five development projects worth around Rs 3,350 crore in Ladakh, covering airport infrastructure, strategic road connectivity, power supply, water conservation and heritage preservation, while stressing that special attention was being given to the Union Territory’s youth. “Our special focus is on the new generation of Ladakh. The youth should receive good education, get opportunities to learn new technology, and not depend on other cities,” Modi said, adding that a major centre of excellence was being established in Leh. Proposals to set up satellite campuses of IIT Jammu and IIM Jammu were also being advanced to improve access to higher education, research and skill development in the region. The projects include a Rs 640-crore passenger terminal at Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport in Leh, spread over 23,800 square metres and designed to handle 35 lakh passengers annually. Equipped with geothermal heating, the terminal is India’s first airport terminal with the facility and aims to improve energy efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. Modi said the modern infrastructure would also give a boost to tourism. He also dedicated the 298-km Nimmu-Padum-Darcha Road, built by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO), connecting Leh with Darcha in Himachal Pradesh through the remote Zanskar Valley. Traversing the high-altitude Shinkun La Pass, the road provides an alternative route to Ladakh alongside the Srinagar-Leh and Manali-Leh highways, strengthening military logistics and improving access to healthcare, education and markets. Modi said a journey that earlier took around 12 hours could now be completed in three. The other projects include the 9 MW Hanu small hydroelectric project and the 66 kV double-circuit Dah-Hanu-Khaltsi transmission line, aimed at improving power supply and strengthening the region’s electricity network. The Prime Minister also inaugurated India’s first Petroglyph Conservation Park at Sindhu Ghat in Leh to preserve prehistoric rock carvings depicting wildlife, human figures and symbolic representations. Under Project Him Sarovar, 40 water bodies developed across 40 villages were inaugurated to conserve water and address seasonal shortages faced by farmers during sowing. The initiative seeks to store water when available and ensure its supply when required, supporting irrigation and long-term water security. Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena said the projects would be milestones in Ladakh’s development, strengthening connectivity, water security, power supply and cultural heritage preservation. “Five new infrastructure projects would prove to be milestones in Ladakh’s development, strengthening connectivity, water security, power supply and preservation of cultural heritage,” Saxena said. He said Ladakh had witnessed significant improvements in infrastructure and living standards since becoming a Union Territory in 2019. Highlighting agricultural progress, he said more than 11,000 greenhouses now enabled farmers to grow vegetables locally and supply them to defence forces through cooperatives. Saxena also highlighted progress in road connectivity, drinking water supply and support for Pashmina herders, and said the completion of the Zojila Tunnel would address a major challenge posed by winter isolation. He urged Modi to inaugurate the tunnel once completed.
